context.title: He Set His Face
context.summary: Jesus sends out the Twelve, feeds five thousand, and Peter confesses him as the Christ. After the transfiguration and further teaching, Jesus resolutely turns toward Jerusalem and warns would-be followers of the cost.
context.background: At the transfiguration Moses and Elijah speak of Jesus' 'decease' (v. 31); the Greek word is exodos, recalling Israel's rescue from Egypt. Verse 51 begins Luke's long journey section, which runs to 19:27. Samaritans and Jews were bitterly divided, so a Samaritan village refuses pilgrims headed for Jerusalem.

customs.note: A ploughman had to keep his eyes ahead to cut a straight furrow. Looking back meant a crooked line. The scene recalls Elisha called from his plough.

watchFor: Herod's question, 'who is this?' (v. 9), is answered by Peter (v. 20).
James and John want to call down fire like Elijah, and Jesus rebukes them (vv. 54–55).
'He stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem' (v. 51).

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.summary: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: John
people.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

places.name: Bethsaida
places.summary: A city near which Christ fed 5,000 (Luke 9:10; comp. John 6:17; Matt. 14:15-21), and where the blind man had his sight restored (Mark 8:22), on the east side of the lake, two miles up the Jordan.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).
